transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Well, I came in because... I just keep feeling like I've ruined things for everybody. I'm in an apprenticeship right now for pipefitting, and I just feel like a total fake. Like I'm letting my family down, and even the younger apprentices. It's usually over stuff that, honestly, I know other people would probably just fix and move on from, but I just can't seem to let it go. I just constantly feel like I'm messing everything up for the people around me.
Do you often feel nervous or on edge?

Um, no, not really. I don't think I feel nervous or, you know, jittery. It's not really an on-edge feeling. It's just more of that constant guilt I was talking about, feeling like I messed up. But no, I wouldn't say I feel anxious.
Do you feel sad most of the time?

Um, no, not really sad. I mean, I don't find myself crying or feeling down in that way. It's really just... like I was saying before, it's more about feeling like a failure or that I'm letting everyone down. But I wouldn't say I feel sad most of the time, no.
Do you find yourself enjoying the things you used to enjoy?

Not really, no. I mean, lately I can just... walk right past my sketchbook and not even pick up a pencil. I've been skipping volleyball, too, and I pretty much just ignore the group texts from my volunteer group. I don't really feel much of anything about it, which is weird, because those used to be the things that actually made me feel like myself. Now I just... don't have any interest in them.
How long have you been feeling this way?

I'd say it's been about nine months. This whole stretch has just... been with me for a while now. It was easier to push through at first, but it definitely got a lot harder to hide once school and my work started slipping.
Have you noticed any significant changes in your weight over the past nine months?

No, I haven't really noticed anything like that. My weight has stayed pretty much the same over the last nine months. I mean, maybe a pound or two fluctuating here and there, but nothing significant at all.
Do you still find pleasure in the activities you're currently doing, like your apprenticeship or spending time with friends?

No, not really. I mean, I still show up to my apprenticeship because I need the hours, but I'm just going through the motions with the pipefitting and everything. I don't get any satisfaction out of it right now. And with my friends... I don't know, it's kind of the same. If I do see them, I'm mostly just sitting there. I wouldn't say I'm actually enjoying myself.
Have you ever thought about hurting yourself?

I don't have some plan to hurt myself or anything like that. But... when I'm driving home after class, or just lying awake in bed, I do get these thoughts. I just think that it would be easier if I didn't wake up tomorrow.
Have you experienced a period of at least two weeks where you felt depressed most of the day?

I don't think so. I mean, I don't really feel sad or depressed most of the day. It's more just that I don't care about things right now, like I was saying. But I wouldn't say I've had a solid two weeks where I actually felt depressed all day, if that makes sense.
Do you feel like you've lost interest in things you used to find pleasurable?

Yeah, I definitely have. Lately, I can just walk right past my sketchbook without even wanting to open it. I've been skipping volleyball, and I just ignore the group texts from my volunteer group. I don't really feel much of anything about missing them, even though those used to be the main things that made me feel like myself. I just don't have the interest right now.
Have you ever had a period where you felt really down or depressed for most of the day, nearly every day?

I think you asked something similar just a minute ago, but no, I really haven't. Like I said, I don't get that sad or down feeling. It's more just... not caring about anything, rather than actually feeling depressed all day.
Have you ever had a time in your life when you felt depressed for most of the day?
No, I haven't. Like I mentioned, I really don't get that sad, depressed feeling. It's just the lack of interest I was talking about.
Have you ever had an episode in the past where you felt depressed for at least two weeks?

No, I really haven't. I know you've asked about this a few different ways now, but my answer is still the same. I've never had a time, whether it was two weeks or longer, where I actually felt depressed. It's just the not caring about stuff that I deal with.
Have you ever had a period in your life that lasted for several months where you felt depressed or down nearly every day?

Honestly, no. I mean... even if we're talking about a few months, it's the same answer. I just don't get sad or down like that. It's strictly just that lack of interest I mentioned before. I've never really felt depressed.
Do you feel like you're unable to experience pleasure from things that would normally bring you happiness?

Yeah, that's exactly it. Like, lately... I can just walk right past my sketchbook and not even care. I've been skipping volleyball, too, and just ignoring all the group texts for my volunteer stuff without really feeling much of anything. And it's weird, because those used to be the things that made me feel like, you know, myself. Now I just don't get anything out of them.
Have you ever had a time in the past when you felt both sad and lost interest in things for at least two weeks?

No, not both of those together. I mean, like I was saying, I definitely get the part where I lose interest in things. But I don't get the sad part along with it. So, no, I've never had a couple of weeks where I felt sad and didn't care at the same time. It's really just always been the not caring.
Have you ever had a time in your life when you felt both very sad and lost interest in things at the same time?
No, I haven't. Like I said just a minute ago, I don't really get sad like that. It's just the losing interest part. So, no, never both at the same time.
Have your feelings of not caring about things been present for most of the day, every day, over the past nine months?

Yeah, pretty much every day. This whole stretch of just... not caring about anything... has been with me for about nine months now. It's been pretty constant the whole time, though I guess it really became a lot harder to hide once my work and school started slipping.
Have you been feeling more tired or having less energy than usual over the past nine months?

No, I haven't really noticed feeling more tired or anything. My energy levels seem pretty normal, honestly. It's just the not caring about stuff that's been the issue, not feeling physically exhausted.
Has your lack of interest in things like sketching, volleyball, and volunteering been consistent over the past nine months?

Yeah, it has been. Lately I can just walk right past my sketchbook, skip volleyball, and ignore the volunteer group texts without feeling much of anything at all. It's strange because those used to be the things that really made me feel like myself, but for the past nine months, that interest just hasn't been there.
